newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Colombian differentials ease.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Colombian differentials ease.

text.p: Colombian differentials continued to soften on the New York physical coffee market this week, despite CSCE futures' recent sharp setback, traders said, but business remained extremely slow.
Lower Colombian differentials, however, did little tempt roasters, whose needs are generally well met through August, they said.
"They're being offered into a void," said one trader. "Roasters do not need nearby coffee and they're offering more than we've seen in a while. Plus Europe and Japan are not buying."

Premiums for Colombian coffees have fallen since Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo announced early last week the country was opening "unlimited" coffee July-August registrations. Ocampo said the country was expected to export 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee.

Colombian MAMs for July-August shipment were heard at 29 cents over CSCE September, compared with 45 cents over last week and 62 cents over two weeks ago. Spot Colombian MAMs garnered some 35 cents over "C", down from 40 cents over heard over a week ago.

Meanwhile, differentials for Brazilian beans have moved out this week in tandem with the pullback in futures. Spot Brazilian Santos 4s were heard at 15 cents under CSCE July, some 5 cents above week ago levels.
CSCE July coffee fell 12.10 cents a lb Friday to settle at 195.70. September ended 9.65 cents lower at 182.75.
Differentials for spot coffee in New York, ex-warehouse, were quoted as follows, all against the CSCE May contract:
Uganda Pmy Robs 8 cts over London 87.61 N
Indonesia EK1 4 cts under London 75.61 N
Ecuador Ext Sup 18 cts under "C" 177.70 N
